comparison.objective: Terminal task selectively opens one named disconnect lever while leaving four neighbors closed; candidate commissions a damper setting and locks it after evaluating repeated axis stops.
comparison.physical_skill: Terminal task uses localized pushing/pulling of one small over-center lever without disturbing adjacent levers. Candidate requires tool alignment and insertion, bimanual counterholding, setscrew manipulation, controlled collar rotation, force-limited locking, and iterative control actuation.
comparison.success_condition: Terminal: target lever ≥80°, all others ≤10°, held 1 s, with partial credit for disturbing neighbors. Candidate: required unlock-adjust-relock process and two compliant dynamic stops without bottoming, rebound, overload, hard-stop contact, or setting drift. Candidate omits numeric rebound, overload, witness-torque, and drift limits; terminal fidelity omits the real knife/contact and uses an unmeasured snap spring.
comparison.reason: Both involve a small rotational control, but selective binary lever actuation does not test tool-mediated locking, continuous adjustment, retention, or dynamic energy-absorption commissioning.
